steps.label: PEAKS & TAILS
steps.sub: Unimodal or bimodal? Extremes rare or common?

eyebrow: Mean vs. median gives away the skew
code:
sym   = pd.Series(rng.normal(50, 10, 5000))
right = pd.Series(rng.exponential(30, 5000))
left  = pd.Series(100 - rng.exponential(10, 5000))

# symmetric:     mean 49.8  median 49.7  skew  0.03
# right-skewed:  mean 30.3  median 21.3  skew  1.97
# left-skewed:   mean 90.0  median 93.0  skew -1.9
caption: Right-skewed: mean > median. Left-skewed: mean < median. |skew| beyond ~1 is strongly skewed.

eyebrow: Kurtosis: how heavy are the tails?
code:
sym.kurt()     # -0.03  -- essentially normal
right.kurt()   #  5.87  -- much heavier tails
left.kurt()    #  4.98
caption: Excess kurtosis: 0 = normal. Noisy on small samples -- treat as a hint, let a chart decide.

eyebrow: When the mean lies: two couriers mixed together
code:
mixed = np.concatenate([rng.normal(20, 4, 2500), rng.normal(60, 4, 2500)])
s = pd.Series(mixed)
s.mean(), s.median()   # ~40.0, ~40.1 -- but almost nobody is near 40!
caption: Only 7 of 5,000 values fell between 32 and 48 -- bimodal data means check for two subgroups.

eyebrow: Fixing strong skew: a log transform
code:
right.skew()             # 1.97
np.log1p(right).skew()   # -0.47  -- much closer to symmetric
caption: log1p compresses a long right tail -- but it changes the units, so interpret carefully.
